repo_statement: M3 / CURRENT_RESULTS section 3 proof route: an eventually nonnegative tail with finite abscissa c has no analytic continuation through c. The repo's proof expands the Taylor series at a=c+r/4 and applies Tonelli.
literature_result: Landau's theorem for Laplace/Mellin integrals: if f>=0 (eventually) and F(s)=int_1^inf f(x)x^{-s}dx/x has finite abscissa sigma_c, then s=sigma_c is a singularity of F. The standard proof uses the same Taylor/positivity argument.
citation: E. Landau, Math. Ann. 61 (1905) 527-550 (Dirichlet-series original). D. V. Widder, The Laplace Transform (1941), Ch. II Thm 5b. Montgomery-Vaughan, Multiplicative Number Theory I (2007), Lemma 15.1. Ingham, The Distribution of Prime Numbers (1932), Thm H. Stated as Proposition 1 in M. Suzuki, arXiv:2411.07436 section 2.4, and as Lemma 2.4 in S. Han, arXiv:2608.27130.
notes: In logarithmic coordinates the hypotheses match: local integrability, eventual nonnegativity, finite abscissa. M3 is this classical theorem, restated for the repo's tail convention on [1,inf). Cite Widder Thm II.5b / MV Lemma 15.1 rather than presenting it as reconstructed mathematics.

repo_statement: M4 + M7 / API.MELLIN.SUBPOWER_NEGATIVE_MASS: if int_1^Y f_-(x)dx/x=O(Y^eps), then M(f_-) is holomorphic on Re s>0. With a fixed noncancelling multiplier, any zero with Re>1/2 is excluded.
literature_result: Classical one-sided Landau oscillation theorems: one-sided bounds of the form A(x) >= -B(x), with B having a holomorphic Mellin transform, force the abscissa singularity onto the real axis. This yields Omega_± and zero-free conclusions (Pólya 1919 for L(x)<=0 => RH; Turán 1948 for L_1; generalized oscillation theorems of Grosswald and Anderson-Stark).
citation: Ingham 1932 Ch. V. Grosswald, Trans. AMS 126 (1967) 1-28 (zbMATH 0155.08602). Anderson-Stark, LNM 899 (1981) 79-106 (zbMATH 0472.10044). Pólya, Jahresber. DMV 28 (1919) 31-40.
notes: Replacing eventual sign by subpower integrated negative mass is a routine corollary: split f=f_+-f_- and apply Landau to f_+. No arXiv abstract stating the 'negative-mass' form explicitly was found (searched 'negative part' AND 'Riemann hypothesis'). The generalization is mild; it is not new analytic mathematics.

repo_statement: Fixed rows 2,3 and the 5:3 scalar: f_j(X)=C_j log X + sum_{n<=X} (p_j*mu)(n) n^{-1/2} log(X/n). This is a first-order logarithmic Riesz mean at critical normalization with Mellin transform [C_j + P_j(s+1/2)/zeta(s+1/2)]/s^2. Eventual sign or negative mass of such a row implies RH.
literature_result: Suzuki (Thm 1): RH <=> sum_{n<=x} Lambda(n)n^{-1/2}log(x/n) - 4sqrt x <= 0 for all large x. The Riesz log-mean has a log-drift main term -(zeta'/zeta)(1/2) log x and an absolutely convergent zero sum. Han (Thm 1.1): f(x)=-sum lambda(n)log n n^{-1/2} log(x/n) >= 0 eventually => RH. Han (Thm 1.2/Cor 1.3): under RH, simple zeros and H3 (sum_gamma |zeta(1+2i gamma)|/(gamma^2|zeta'(1/2+i gamma)|)<inf), f(x) ~ (log x)^3/(12|zeta(1/2)|), so f is eventually positive.
citation: M. Suzuki, 'On variants of Chebyshev's conjecture', arXiv:2411.07436 (2024; v3 2025), Thm 1. S. Han, 'On variants of Pólya's conjecture', arXiv:2608.27130 (27 Aug 2026), Thms 1.1, 1.2, Cor 1.3.
notes: This is the same detector pattern: a critical n^{-1/2} weight, log(x/n) Riesz smoothing, Landau consumer for the sign direction, and an explicit-formula converse needing simple zeros plus a zeta' summability hypothesis. The repo's rows use 1/zeta times a finite Dirichlet polynomial instead of zeta'/zeta or zeta(2s)/zeta(s). Suzuki 2024 predates the repo's L-96000 (2026-08-16); Han is contemporaneous. The analyst computed the drifts kappa_j = C_j + P_j(1/2)/zeta(1/2): kappa_2=1.11171, kappa_3=0.40646, kappa_W=6.77792. A non-directed float scan to X=10^7 gives f/log X equal to 1.1091, 0.4029 and 6.7541 at X=10^7, and no negative values on [1,10^7]. This is exploratory and finite.

repo_statement: Fixed critical detectors whose eventual sign implies RH (rows, 5:3, C_m, H^{[1]}).
literature_result: Historical sign criteria implying RH: Pólya's L(x)<=0 (1919), Turán's L_1(x)>0 (1948), Mertens |M(x)|<sqrt x. Johnston proved RH <=> int_2^x (pi(t)-li(t))dt<0 for all x>2. Mossinghoff-Trudgian treat the weighted family L_alpha.
citation: D. R. Johnston, Canad. Math. Bull. 66 (2023) 185-195 (arXiv:2201.06184). Mossinghoff-Trudgian, Int. J. Number Theory 17 (2021) 1697-1716 (arXiv:2007.14537). Mossinghoff-Trudgian, J. Aust. Math. Soc. 93 (2012) 157-171.
notes: Johnston's equivalence is quoted in Suzuki's introduction. The Pólya/Turán/Ingham history was read in the Mossinghoff-Trudgian 2020 introduction.

repo_statement: R17: the negative-mass criterion for C_m is necessary as well as sufficient. RH gives sum beta(n) n^{-s} partial sums O(x^{1/2+eps}), and Abel summation then makes each term O(X^eps).
literature_result: Littlewood (1912): RH <=> M(x)=O(x^{1/2+eps}). More generally inf{alpha: M(x)=O(x^alpha)}=Theta, and partial summation transfers this to every fixed bounded-variation smoothing.
citation: J. E. Littlewood, C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris 154 (1912) 263-266. Titchmarsh, Theory of the Riemann Zeta-Function, 2nd ed., section 14.25.
notes: The same argument applies verbatim to rows 2,3, W_X and any detector C log X + sum (p*mu)(n)n^{-1/2}K(X/n) with finite p and a fixed BV kernel. So OPEN.ARITH.ROWS23_NATIVE (negative-mass branch), OPEN.ARITH.FIVE_THREE_NEGATIVE_MASS and OPEN.ARITH.FIXED_DETECTOR_NEGATIVE_MASS are RH-equivalent, not merely sufficient.

repo_statement: R15 / ARITH.WAVELET.SPECTRAL_ABSCISSA: |1/zeta(w)| << |t|^eps for Re w>=a>Theta, and the weighted L2/Hardy abscissa of the compact Möbius wavelet is Theta+1/2 as an infimum.
literature_result: Titchmarsh's Thm 14.2 proves 1/zeta = O(t^eps) for sigma>=1/2+delta under RH, using Borel-Caratheodory and Hadamard three-circles. Replacing 1/2 by Theta gives the same proof. The classical abscissa statements say the convergence/growth abscissa of sum mu(n)n^{-s} and M(x) equals Theta. Mellin-Plancherel / Paley-Wiener gives the L2 version.
citation: Titchmarsh, Theory of the Riemann Zeta-Function, 2nd ed., sections 14.2 and 14.25-14.29.
notes: The repo's statement is a compactly smoothed version with the correct infimum and nonattainment qualifications. The reciprocal-growth step (R15 part 1) is essentially Titchmarsh 14.2 with Theta in place of 1/2. Cite it.

repo_statement: R4 literal MWOC criterion: a suffix field A_X(r) in H=L^2([1/8,1],2r dr), a fixed countable dense test family, and Mellin duality separating reciprocal-zeta poles.
literature_result: Nyman-Beurling criterion: RH <=> chi_(0,1] lies in the closed span of dilated fractional parts rho(theta/x) in L^2. Báez-Duarte (2002) shows natural dilations suffice. Báez-Duarte notes the unconditional lower bound ||F-chi|| >= C/sqrt(log N) for N-term approximants, sharpened by Burnol.
citation: L. Báez-Duarte, arXiv:math/0202141 (Rend. Mat. Acc. Lincei 2003), Thm 1.1 and eq. (1.2). J.-F. Burnol, Adv. Math. 170 (2002) 56-70. B. Nyman (thesis 1950); A. Beurling, PNAS 41 (1955).
notes: Both use L^2 dilation structure plus Mellin duality. The repo's criterion is an energy/subpower growth statement, not an approximation/density statement, so it is not equivalent as stated. Cite Nyman-Beurling as the closest classical relative.

repo_statement: Cauchy-Poisson energy at tau=1: sum d_m d_n min(m,n)/max(m,n), i.e. the Cauchy weight with Fourier transform e^{-|log(m/n)|}.
literature_result: Balazard-Saias-Yor: int_{Re s=1/2} log|zeta(s)| |ds|/|s|^2 = 2pi sum_{beta>1/2} log|rho/(1-rho)|, so RH <=> the integral is 0. This is a single nonnegative functional with the same Cauchy-type weight |ds|/|s|^2 used in the Nyman-Beurling/Báez-Duarte Hilbert-space computations.
citation: Balazard, Saias, Yor, Adv. Math. 143 (1999) 284-287. Statement verified in Bui-Lester-Milinovich, arXiv:1306.0856, eqs. (1.1)-(1.2).
notes: This overlaps in weight/Gram structure only. Neither criterion implies the other at the repo's normalization.

repo_statement: Q4 signed mean value: int_{-T}^T|sum_{m<=X} c_m m^{-it}|^2 dt <= (2T+14X) sum|c_m|^2, proved by comparison with the continuous Hilbert transform.
literature_result: Montgomery-Vaughan via the generalized Hilbert inequality: int_0^T|sum a_n n^{-it}|^2 dt = sum |a_n|^2 (T+O(n)), with per-coefficient error.
citation: H. L. Montgomery, R. C. Vaughan, 'Hilbert's inequality', J. London Math. Soc. (2) 8 (1974) 73-82, DOI 10.1112/jlms/s2-8.1.73 (already cited in reviews/D-pass3/EXTERNAL_INPUTS.md).
notes: The repo's bound is the uniform-X special case with an explicit constant 14. MV gives the sharper per-coefficient O(n) form. The explicit MV/Preissmann constant was not compared.

repo_statement: Q4.JORDAN_PERIODIZED: the complete-residue periodized carry covariance is (gcd(d,e)^2-1)/(4de), giving a Jordan-2 GCD-square positive Gram with a squared-logarithmic bound.
literature_result: Franel's formula: int_0^1 ((mx))((nx)) dx = gcd(m,n)^2/(12mn), stated by Franel and proved by Landau (1924) in connection with the Franel-Landau Farey/RH criterion. Gál's theorem and Aistleitner-Berkes-Seip give optimal bounds for GCD sums sum c_k c_l gcd(n_k,n_l)^{2alpha}/(n_k n_l)^alpha; for alpha=1 the extremal growth is (log log N)^2.
citation: Aistleitner-Berkes-Seip, 'GCD sums from Poisson integrals and systems of dilated functions', JEMS 17 (2015), arXiv:1210.0741 (Franel formula at their eq. after (30)). J. Franel and E. Landau, Gött. Nachr. 1924. I. S. Gál, Nieuw Arch. Wisk. 23 (1949).
notes: The repo's covariance looks like a discrete/periodized analogue of Franel's integral, with a -1 discretization correction and different normalization. The exact correspondence at the repo normalization was not verified. Applies only to the periodized ensemble, not the physical fixed-endpoint measure.

repo_statement: ARITH.VAUGHAN.LARGE_DIVISOR and ARITH.XD.SAME_K1_TRANSLATION: the balanced Vaughan remainder is a large-divisor Hankel bilinear form. Largest-prime and Vaughan forms agree modulo an L1(dX/X) error on the same kernel.
literature_result: Vaughan's identity for mu, 1/zeta = 2M - zeta M^2 + (1/zeta)(1-zeta M)^2 with M a truncated Dirichlet polynomial of mu, splits sums of mu into Type I and Type II bilinear forms sum a_m b_n f(mn) (Hankel in log coordinates). Heath-Brown's generalized identity gives finer decompositions.
citation: R. C. Vaughan, C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris 285 (1977) 981-983. D. R. Heath-Brown, Canad. J. Math. 34 (1982) 1365-1377. Iwaniec-Kowalski, Analytic Number Theory, section 13.4.
notes: The repo's exact sign, squarefree and gcd constraints and same-kernel bookkeeping are source-specific. The underlying decomposition is classical.

repo_statement: Half-divisor sequence eta(p^k)=binom(2k,k)/4^k with eta*eta=1.
literature_result: These are the Dirichlet coefficients of zeta(s)^{1/2}, d_{1/2}(n), since (1-x)^{-1/2}=sum binom(2k,k)4^{-k}x^k. They are treated by the Selberg-Delange method.
citation: G. Tenenbaum, Introduction to Analytic and Probabilistic Number Theory, Ch. II.5 (Selberg-Delange).
notes: Cite d_{1/2} / zeta^{1/2}. The weighted Hardy-inequality constant ('Hardy norm 3') should be cited to Hardy-Littlewood-Pólya, Inequalities, Thms 327-330, at the exact weight used.

repo_statement: Excursion estimate R7: int_I f_- <= |I|^{3/2}||f'||_{L2(I)}/pi on each interior excursion with zero endpoint values, then Cauchy-Schwarz.
literature_result: Wirtinger's inequality: for f(0)=f(l)=0, int_0^l f^2 <= (l/pi)^2 int_0^l f'^2.
citation: Hardy-Littlewood-Pólya, Inequalities (1934), Thm 257.
notes: The constant pi^{-1} matches. The both-boundary correction is a bookkeeping repair.

repo_statement: A-M03: the no-real-main-term wavelet changes sign arbitrarily late in both directions, unconditionally.
literature_result: Pólya (1930) and Kaczorowski-Pintz show that if the Mellin transform is regular on the real axis but singular at ±i gamma, then f has at least c(f) log Y sign changes in (0,Y]. For psi(x)-x, liminf V(T)/log T >= gamma_1/pi + 1/60 (Grześkowiak-Kaczorowski-Pańkowski-Radziejewski, Math. Comp. 2025).
citation: Kaczorowski-Pintz, Acta Math. Hungar. 48 (1986) 173-185 (Zbl 0613.10036); 49 (1987) 441-453 (Zbl 0631.10026). G. Pólya, Gött. Nachr. 1930, 19-27. Kaczorowski, Acta Arith. 44 (1984), 45 (1985). arXiv:2408.10399; arXiv:1910.14203.
notes: The repo proves infinitely many sign changes. The literature gives >> log Y sign changes for the same singularity configuration.

repo_statement: Carry hinge: q^{-1/2}-T^{-1/2} as a positive mixture of hinges (K+1-q)_+; linear-hinge responses of the arithmetic source.
literature_result: Every convex function is an affine function plus a positive mixture of hinges (second-difference representation). Hinge (x-n)_+ responses of a sequence are first-order Riesz (Cesàro) means, e.g. sum mu(n)(x-n)_+ = int_0^x M(t)dt. Classical Riesz-mean theory (Hardy-Riesz 1915) shows every fixed Riesz order of sum mu(n)n^{-s} has the same abscissa Theta.
citation: G. H. Hardy, M. Riesz, The General Theory of Dirichlet's Series (1915). K. Chandrasekharan, S. Minakshisundaram, Typical Means (1952).
notes: The signed square-root-weighted response target is not in the literature as such.

obstruction: Ingham's linear-relations theorem. If M(x)/sqrt x or L(x)/sqrt x is bounded on one side, then RH and simple zeros hold, and the positive ordinates satisfy infinitely many integer linear relations. Under LI, liminf x^{-1/2}M(x) = -inf and limsup = +inf.
citation: A. E. Ingham, 'On two conjectures in the theory of numbers', Amer. J. Math. 64 (1942) 313-319 (zbMATH 0063.02974 review). Restated in Mossinghoff-Trudgian arXiv:2007.14537 section 1.
how_it_constrains: It rules out, under LI, pointwise eventual sign for 'Pólya-class' critical detectors: those with only a constant main term and zero coefficients r_gamma ~ 1/(gamma zeta'(rho)) that are not absolutely summable. The repo's SHARP critical H^{[1]} with jump kernel T(y)=4sqrt y-3 is in this class. Its Mellin transform B(s+1/2)(4/(s-1/2)-3/s) gives bias -3B(1/2)=1.80332 and r_gamma ~ (1-67^{-rho})/(i gamma zeta'(rho)). Analyst computation: sum over the first 200 zeros of 2|r_gamma| is 1.426 and still growing, tracking the Mertens analogue (1.393). Under RH plus Gonek's second-moment asymptotic, Hölder gives sum 1/|rho zeta'(rho)| = inf. So 'H^{[1]}(x)>0 for all large x' would force linear relations among zeta ordinates. Only the negative-mass/weighted-variation form (OPEN.ARITH.CV) is viable. The obstruction does NOT apply to detectors with log drift (rows 2,3, W_X) or with absolutely summable gamma^{-2} coefficients and a large bias (G_1 with S=4(sqrt y-1)_+: bias 2.40443 vs sum 2|r| ~ 0.066 over 200 zeros; C_m).
evidence_level: abstract_only (zbMATH review) + secondary_source (Mossinghoff-Trudgian intro). The application to H^{[1]} is analyst derivation plus non-directed mpmath numerics and is not reviewed.

obstruction: Pólya-, Turán- and Mertens-type fixed sign conjectures, each implying RH through a Landau consumer, are false.
citation: C. B. Haselgrove, Mathematika 5 (1958) 141-145 (Zbl 0085.27102). Odlyzko-te Riele, J. reine angew. Math. 357 (1985). Tanaka, Tokyo J. Math. 3 (1980). Borwein-Ferguson-Mossinghoff, Math. Comp. 77 (2008). Kim-Nguyen, arXiv:2502.21021 (first Mertens counterexample below exp(1.96e19)). Humphries, arXiv:1108.1524 (under RH+LI, positive log density of Pólya counterexamples).
how_it_constrains: Positivity observed up to large X, such as the repo's row scans or historical L(x)<=0 up to 9e8, is no evidence for a fixed detector's eventual sign when it lies in the Pólya class. The repo's preference for the subpower negative-mass premise over pointwise sign is consistent with this history.

obstruction: The negative-mass premise is RH-equivalent for every fixed detector in the repo's class, so OPEN_CUTS section 1 cannot be weaker than RH. Graded form: for theta in (0,1/2), int_1^Y F_-dx/x << Y^{theta+eps} for a fixed noncancelling detector excludes zeros with Re rho > 1/2+theta. Conversely, a zero-free half-plane Re s>1/2+theta gives |F(X)| << X^{theta+eps} for 1/s^2-smoothed rows, via Titchmarsh 14.2-type reciprocal bounds and Mellin inversion.
citation: Littlewood 1912. Titchmarsh sections 14.2 and 14.25. Landau / MV Lemma 15.1. Repo R17 (reviews/D-final/REPAIRS.md) and R15 part 1 for the reciprocal bound.
how_it_constrains: Any unconditional partial result with theta<1/2 would be a zeta zero-free strip, which no one has ever established (the best known regions are of Vinogradov-Korobov type). Partial 'Y^theta negative mass' results in the Q4, half-divisor, XD or wavelet coordinates are therefore at least as hard as quasi-RH.
evidence_level: memory_unverified (classical); the graded equivalence is an analyst derivation to be reviewed

obstruction: Sign-change counts are Theta(log Y) for no-main-term detectors. Kaczorowski-Pintz show V(f,Y) >= c log Y whenever the Mellin transform has a nonreal boundary singularity but is regular on the real axis. Under RH the logarithmic horizon caps the count at O(log Y).
citation: Kaczorowski-Pintz 1986/87 (Zbl 0613.10036, 0631.10026). Morrill-Platt-Trudgian arXiv:1910.14203. Grześkowiak et al. arXiv:2408.10399.
how_it_constrains: This supports the OPEN_CUTS firewall: counting negative intervals of the wavelet or XD detectors cannot distinguish RH from not-RH. L(Y) <= log Y is automatic, as R7 already notes.

obstruction: Finite truncations of L^2 RH criteria have unconditional logarithmic defects: for N-term Nyman-Beurling approximants, ||F-chi|| >= C/sqrt(log N), with Burnol's sharper constant.
citation: Báez-Duarte arXiv:math/0202141 eq. (1.2), citing Balazard-Saias and Burnol (Adv. Math. 170 (2002)).
how_it_constrains: Any fixed-cutoff or finite-window positive or energy certificate in the wavelet suffix-field Hilbert space can approach a criterion at best logarithmically. This is consistent with the repo's REFUTATION.WAVELET.CRITICAL_DESMOOTHING and finite-scope firewalls.

obstruction: The Landau-Pintz finite-to-zero-free method cannot improve knowledge for zeta. Johnston-Trudgian call it 'doomed to fail' for zeta, because RH is verified to height 3e12 and explicit zero-free regions are already strong.
citation: D. R. Johnston, T. Trudgian, 'A round of Pintz to celebrate oscillations in sums', arXiv:2511.09978 (v4 2026), section 1. Pintz, Math. Pannonica 28 (2022) 58-64 (Zbl 1513.11159).
how_it_constrains: A finite negative-mass computation for rows 2,3, W_X or C_m, converted by an explicit Landau-Pintz theorem, yields only zero-free information weaker than existing verification. It cannot serve as evidence toward the subpower premise.

obstruction: Family averages of sign criteria can be proved unconditionally while the principal member stays RH-hard. Suzuki proves unconditional negativity of character-averaged weighted Chebyshev Riesz sums for Q >= x, while the individual sign is equivalent to (G)RH.
citation: M. Suzuki arXiv:2411.07436, Thm 7 versus Thms 1 and 3.
how_it_constrains: This reinforces the repo's principal-member firewall (OPEN_CUTS section 5): a family-averaged negative-mass bound does not supply the fixed principal detector premise.

obstruction: Selberg's parity phenomenon: sieve or positive-weight (Type I) information alone cannot produce cancellation in mu or lambda sums.
citation: A. Selberg, Proc. Sympos. Pure Math. 20 (1971). Friedlander-Iwaniec, Opera de Cribro (2010).
how_it_constrains: This is a heuristic counterpart of the repo's positive-floor-kernel, positive-divisor-compiler and source-blind-convexity refutations. Positive kernels or positive inverses cannot by themselves yield the signed critical estimate. Genuine Type II (bilinear) signed input is needed, as in the HCNC, XD and UOSACF gates.

tool: An explicit-formula converse for log-Riesz detectors with drift (Han 2026, Thm 1.2 method; Suzuki 2024, Thm 1 method).
citation: S. Han arXiv:2608.27130 section 3. M. Suzuki arXiv:2411.07436 section 3. Titchmarsh section 14.16 (good contours T_nu).
target_gap: Classify the open nodes OPEN.ARITH.ROWS23_NATIVE and OPEN.ARITH.FIVE_THREE_NEGATIVE_MASS: are they strictly stronger than RH or equivalent to it?
precise_next_step: Compute the double pole at s=0 of C_j/s^2+P_j(s+1/2)/(s^2 zeta(s+1/2)), which gives f_j(X) = kappa_j log X + kappa'_j + Phi_j(log X) + o(1). Here kappa_j = C_j+P_j(1/2)/zeta(1/2), and Phi_j(t)=2Re sum_gamma P_j(rho)e^{i gamma t}/((rho-1/2)^2 zeta'(rho)) under RH and simple zeros. Then verify Han-type truncation with H3' := sum_gamma 1/(gamma^2|zeta'(1/2+i gamma)|) < inf. Analyst values: kappa_2=1.11171, kappa_3=0.40646, kappa_W=6.77792, all positive. This makes eventual sign of rows 2,3 and W_X equivalent to RH modulo simple zeros and H3'.
risk: Gives no unconditional progress. It only removes the possibility that the sign premise is 'stronger than RH' under standard conjectures. The kappa values come from non-directed floating point and must be recomputed with directed arithmetic before canonical use.

tool: A graded Landau consumer combined with reciprocal-zeta growth inside a zero-free half-plane.
citation: Titchmarsh section 14.2 (proof method); the repo's R15 part 1; MV Lemma 15.1.
target_gap: Calibrate OPEN_CUTS section 1: what does a non-subpower but nontrivial negative-mass bound buy?
precise_next_step: State and prove: for a fixed noncancelling detector, int_1^Y F_- dx/x << Y^{theta+eps} for all eps implies zeta(s) != 0 for Re s > 1/2+theta. For the 1/s^2-smoothed rows, add the converse direction by shifting the Mellin inversion contour to Re s = theta+delta, using |1/zeta| << t^eps there. Register it as a separate graded API node.
risk: No risk to correctness. It makes explicit that any theta<1/2 result would be a zero-free strip, i.e. quasi-RH, so it reframes but does not close the gap.

tool: Ingham's Fejér-kernel method plus Haselgrove/Odlyzko-te Riele/Hurst lattice-reduction search.
citation: Ingham 1942. Haselgrove 1958. Odlyzko-te Riele 1985. G. Hurst, Math. Comp. 87 (2018) (arXiv:1610.08551). Kim-Nguyen arXiv:2502.21021.
target_gap: OPEN_CUTS section 1 'concrete output: a counterexample to a proposed intermediate bound', applied to any proposed pointwise eventual positivity of Pólya-class critical detectors such as SHARP H^{[1]} with T=4sqrt y-3.
precise_next_step: Compute certified r_gamma = (4/(rho-1)-3/(rho-1/2))(1-67^{-rho})/zeta'(rho) for the first 10^4 or more zeros. Use LLL/BKZ to find y with c + 2 Re sum_{gamma<T}(1-gamma/T) r_gamma e^{i gamma y} < 0, where c = -3(1-67^{-1/2})/zeta(1/2) = 1.80332. As in Haselgrove, this would unconditionally refute 'H^{[1]}>=0 eventually', because that hypothesis itself implies RH and simple zeros.
risk: It needs Fejér-weighted alignment exceeding 1.80, comparable to Hurst's limsup M(x)/sqrt x >= 1.826, so it may need many zeros. It refutes only a pointwise statement that the repo does not currently claim as a target, and leaves OPEN.ARITH.CV untouched.

tool: B^2-almost-periodic limiting distributions for explicit-formula functions (Akbary-Ng-Shahabi, Thm 1.2 / Cor 1.3; Rubinstein-Sarnak; Humphries).
citation: Akbary-Ng-Shahabi arXiv:1306.1657, Thm 1.2 and Cor 1.3. Rubinstein-Sarnak, Exp. Math. 3 (1994). Humphries arXiv:1108.1524.
target_gap: Predict the size of V(Y) and B_partial(Y) in the corrected excursion estimate (CURRENT_RESULTS section 3) for each fixed detector under RH+LI, and decide which detectors have log-density-zero negative sets.
precise_next_step: For each detector, write phi(y)=F(e^y)-(drift) = c + Re sum r_n e^{i lambda_n y} + E. Check the coefficient conditions of ANS Cor 1.3(a): r_gamma << gamma^{-beta} with beta > 1/2 holds for 1/s^2 rows and the wavelet under |zeta'(rho)|^{-1} << |rho|^{1/2-eps}. Compute the limiting distribution's mass below 0 to classify detectors into drift, bias or Pólya classes.
risk: Conditional on RH, LI and negative-moment hypotheses. It is heuristic for the unconditional premise and gives no proof.

tool: Explicit Landau-Pintz mean-value Omega theorem.
citation: Johnston-Trudgian arXiv:2511.09978, Thm 1. Pintz, Math. Pannonica 28 (2022). Pintz, Acta Arith. 42 (1982) and 43 (1984) (Zbl 0469.10019, 0544.10048).
target_gap: Turn the repo's finite computations (row scans, finite negative-mass certificates) into an honest, quantified implication. This is the 'bounded contribution' type in OPEN_CUTS.
precise_next_step: Instantiate JT Thm 1 with A=f_j, F=P_j(s+1/2), G=s^2 zeta(s+1/2)-type factorization. Output an explicit lower bound for (1/Y) int_1^Y |f_j - main| in terms of any hypothetical simple zero beta_0+i gamma_0, then compare with a certified finite scan. Kaczorowski-Pintz one-sided variants would be needed for f_- rather than |f|.
risk: The authors state that for zeta this cannot beat existing RH verification to 3e12. Its value is calibration and firewall, not progress.

tool: Gál / Aistleitner-Berkes-Seip GCD-sum bounds, together with Franel-Landau.
target_gap: Q4.JORDAN_PERIODIZED 'positive Gram with squared-logarithmic bound' in the periodized ensemble.
precise_next_step: Rewrite (gcd(d,e)^2-1)/(4de) as (1/3) times the Franel kernel plus a rank-one-type correction. Apply Gál's optimal (log log N)^2 bound for alpha=1 GCD quadratic forms to see whether the periodized log^2 bound improves to (log log)^2.
risk: Applies only to the periodized model. The repo's own firewall says it does not transfer to the physical fixed-endpoint measure, and it does not touch the signed coarse modes.

repo_statement: Energy-Schur reduction (CURRENT_RESULTS §7; OPERATOR_AUDIT O4): with a coercive infinite sector, full-window positivity iff a finite Schur complement S is PSD, and the negative indices are equal.
literature_result: Lemma 8.16: let Q on L2([λ^{-1},λ],d*u) split as V⊕W with dim V<∞ and D ≥ d||w||^2, d>0, on W. With S(v)=A(v)-||D^{-1/2}B*v||^2, Q ≥ 0 iff S ≥ 0, and inf Q/||ψ||^2 ≥ min(0, λ_min(S)). Proposition 8.17: ε_λ is nonincreasing in λ, and ε_λ ≥ -η(λ) with η→0 for all large λ already forces ε_λ ≥ 0 for every λ, which is RH. Proposition 8.18 reduces RH (conditionally on (H2′), (R1), (R2)) to the sign of S on a transition-and-pole block of dimension O(Aσ^2 log λ)+2.
citation: R. Andrews, A. Connes, A. La Gatta, 'The uncertainty operator, the Weil ground state and the zeros of zeta...', arXiv:2611.13129 (Nov 2026), §8.6, Lemma 8.16, Props 8.17–8.18, Thm 8.14
notes: Same architecture for the standard Weil form QW_λ on multiplicative windows. The repo's version needs only a form-norm (primitive ||φ'||) coercivity, not an L2 gap; its Riesz vectors may lie outside L2; it adds negative-index equality, Galerkin monotonicity and a two-sided residual enclosure. In that coercivity hypothesis the repo is more general; ACL is more advanced on the conditioning (prolate vectors). Kernels and normalizations differ (repo: Lorentz-weighted b/(b^2+w^2) damped kernel).

repo_statement: O2: on an explicit finite-codimension subspace (K+3 constraints) the window form is coercive, and the negative index on each window is finite.
literature_result: Yoshida studied QW on localized spaces. Per secondary sources: positivity for sufficiently small support [Lemma 2]; positivity on subspaces K_N(a) of finite codimension [Lemma 3]; RH equivalent to nondegeneracy on the completion [Thm 2]; QW ≥ 0 on all odd test functions implies RH [Prop. 1]. Connes–Consani attribute to Yoshida (their ref. [34]) the archimedean positivity for support in (1/2,2), proved by explicit computation.
citation: H. Yoshida, 'On Hermitian forms attached to zeta functions', Zeta Functions in Geometry (Tokyo 1990), Adv. Stud. Pure Math. 21 (1992) 281–325; Zbl 0817.11041. As summarized in M. Suzuki, arXiv:2606.09096 §1.1 and Connes–Consani arXiv:2006.13771 p.2
notes: The repo's O2 is a quantitative, explicit-rational version (K=101 at L=1) for a different, Lorentz-weighted kernel. Cite Yoshida as the origin of finite-codimension positivity of localized Weil forms.

repo_statement: Finite negative index of the window form, and Galerkin truncations as approximations to it (O4: S_m ↓ S).
literature_result: The infimum of Weil's functional on the unit sphere of L2[-t,t] is attained. Finite truncations of the Fourier-side quadratic form are studied. If RH fails with only finitely many off-line zeros, large truncations have exactly half that many negative eigenvalues. Suzuki 2026 notes that Bombieri's continuity-in-support claim ([1, Thm 5]) 'calls for a more careful analysis' and proves continuity of the lowest eigenvalue (Suzuki Thm 1.3).
citation: E. Bombieri, 'Remarks on Weil's quadratic functional in the theory of prime numbers I', Rend. Lincei Mat. Appl. (9) 11 (2000) 183–233, Zbl 1008.11034; E. Bombieri, 'A variational approach to the explicit formula', CPAM 56 (2003) 1151–1164; Suzuki arXiv:2606.09096 Thm 1.3
notes: Bombieri's negative-eigenvalue count gives a concrete prediction for the repo's negative-index identity: neg-index(S_L) should equal (number of off-line zeros)/2 for large L, under a finiteness hypothesis. Hypotheses of the count were not checked from full text.

repo_statement: The localized window form is closed and bounded below, with a coercive infinite-dimensional positive sector (qualitative part of O2/O4).
literature_result: [CCM, Thm 3.6, Cor 3.7]: QW^a is lower bounded and closed, and defines a self-adjoint A_a with discrete spectrum bounded below and a ground state. A_a is the Friedrichs extension of D*G_aD, where G_a is the compressed integral operator of Suzuki's continuous screw function g. The lowest eigenvalue λ_a is continuous in a, and for small a it is positive, simple and even.
citation: A. Connes, C. Consani, H. Moscovici, 'Zeta spectral triples', arXiv:2511.22755 (EMS Ser. Lect. Math. 37, 2026), Thm 3.6; M. Suzuki, 'Weil's quadratic form via the screw function', arXiv:2606.09096 (2026), Thms 1.1, 1.3, 1.4
notes: Suzuki writes the Weil form as derivatives of test functions against a continuous twice-integrated kernel. This parallels the repo's O3 coupling q(v,z)=b⟨φ_v',F_z⟩ with W in W^{1,1}. CCM Thm 3.6 itself was read only via Suzuki's summary.

repo_statement: The open 'rigorous continuum lower certificate' for a single window (L=1), and the bounded contribution 'a whole-window sign certificate'.
literature_result: For the standard Weil form, a certified computation gives Q(f) ≥ 8.9×10^-18 ||f||^2 for all real even f with supp f ⊆ [-0.8,0.8] (autocorrelation support 1.6), and 8.2×10^-15 in the odd sector. Method: a pointwise envelope above a threshold T♯ (Thm 1.1) reduces the whole window to PSD of one Legendre-basis matrix, with tail deviation and coupling below 10^-100. Ingredients are verified Cholesky, a Bernstein-ellipse quadrature bound and a forbidden-region tail bound. Certified variational upper bounds give 8.9e-18 ≤ λ*(0.8) ≤ 2.27e-17, and λ*(0.5) is about 1e-6.
citation: X. Zhu, 'Weil positivity in compact windows: a finite reduction, certified two-sided bounds, and a Landau–Widom decay law', arXiv:2608.24827v2 (2026), Thms 1.1, 1.2, Cor 6.3, Table 3
notes: This is a different form: standard Weil Q without the Lorentz weight and damping, so it does NOT certify the repo's S_L. It does show that a support of length 1.6 (beyond the repo's L=1, autocorrelation [-1,1]) is certifiable for the classical form, with a reusable certificate pipeline. Unrefereed preprint; its earlier support-2.38 claim was retracted by the author.

repo_statement: Constrained positivity of the archimedean-dominated form (moments against e^{±ct} remove the pole; digamma increments positive).
literature_result: For g in C_c^∞ supported in [2^{-1/2},2^{1/2}] with ĝ vanishing at i/2 and 0, W_∞(g*g*) ≥ Tr(ϑ(g)Sϑ(g)*) ≥ 0 (Theorem 1), with a refined version allowing a -c|ĝ(0)|^2 correction (Thm 6.11). This gives archimedean Weil positivity at log-length log 2 via prolate functions and the Sonin space.
citation: A. Connes, C. Consani, 'Weil positivity and trace formula, the archimedean place', Selecta Math. 27 (2021) Paper 77, arXiv:2006.13771, Theorem 1, Thm 6.11
notes: Same role as the repo's pole/moment constraints and O2 coercivity. The repo's window L=1 includes prime 2, so it lies beyond this archimedean-only range.

repo_statement: Galerkin effective matrices are upper approximations; finite positive sections are not lower certificates (O4; REFUTATIONS §3).
literature_result: For the Connes–van Suijlekom/CCM Galerkin truncation at prime cutoff c and band N, every quadratic value is an exact zero sum (Thm 2.5). The omitted archimedean tail is a totally positive Cauchy–Stieltjes increment (Thm 3.2). Two-sided rule (Cor 3.3): finite-T positivity certifies cutoff-free positivity of the band-N truncation; an eigenvalue below -B_T certifies a negative; eigenvalues in [-B_T,0) certify nothing. Interval LDL^T resolves tiny scales directly.
citation: A. Groskin, 'A finite Guinand–Weil dictionary and archimedean tail order for the truncated Weil quadratic form', arXiv:2607.02828v3 (2026), Thm 2.5, Thm 3.2, Cor 3.3
notes: Groskin certifies a fixed finite band, not the continuum window. This is consistent with the repo's insistence that band positivity is not a continuum lower certificate. Unrefereed.

repo_statement: Negative-index equality between the full window form and the Schur complement S (O4.1).
literature_result: Haynsworth inertia additivity: for a Hermitian block matrix with invertible block C, In(M)=In(C)+In(M/C). Its form-theoretic analogue is the Feshbach/Schur complement map.
citation: E. V. Haynsworth, 'Determination of the inertia of a partitioned Hermitian matrix', Linear Algebra Appl. 1 (1968) 73–81
notes: The repo proves an energy-space, infinite-dimensional version (C positive but unbounded inverse, Riesz vectors outside L2). Equality of nullities correctly is not claimed.

repo_statement: Cardinal capture (R16): under an off-line zero packet there are compact smooth test functions whose Weil value tends to -2m.
literature_result: Weil (1952): T(f*f̄*) is positive semidefinite iff RH, over C_c^∞ test functions. The necessity direction constructs a compactly supported test with negative value from an off-line zero. Bombieri (2000) revisits it variationally.
citation: A. Weil, 'Sur les formules explicites de la théorie des nombres premiers', Comm. Sém. Math. Univ. Lund (1952) 252–265; Bombieri 2000 (Zbl 1008.11034 review)
notes: The repo's version is multiplicity-aware and gives exact interpolation with explicit topologies. This is a careful re-proof of the classical converse, appropriately labelled 'capture', not a positivity result.

repo_statement: L-91035: Suzuki's completed Hankel operator gives the explicit amplitude-level scattering isometry for a>1/2.
literature_result: Proposition 2.1: Mellin identity for h_ω. Theorem 2.2: criterion for Θ_ω(z)=ξ(1/2-ω-iz)/ξ(1/2+ω-iz) to be meromorphic inner. Lemma 4.1: if Θ_ω is inner, H_ω extends to an isometry of L2((0,∞),dx). Θ_ω is inner for ω ≥ 1/2 unconditionally and for 0<ω<1/2 under RH, by Lagarias.
citation: M. Suzuki, 'A canonical system of differential equations arising from the Riemann zeta-function', arXiv:1204.1827v2, Prop 2.1, Thm 2.2, Lemma 4.1, §1; J. C. Lagarias, 'Zero spacing distributions for differenced L-functions', Acta Arith. 120 (2005)
notes: This pins the primary source requested by the packet's required fix. The repo's c_a(n)=n^aΣ_{d|n}μ(d)d^{-2a} matches Suzuki's c_ω(n).

repo_statement: T-91008 equivalence 'RH iff delayed first-chaos Gram ⪰ 0' depends on Suzuki's screw criterion.
literature_result: The explicit continuous even function g (Suzuki's screw function) is a screw function in the Krein–Langer sense, i.e. g(t-u)-g(t)-g(-u)+g(0) is nonnegative definite, iff RH. Under RH, the completion of C_c^∞ in the Weil form is isomorphic to a de Branges space.
citation: M. Suzuki, 'Aspects of the screw function corresponding to the Riemann zeta function', J. London Math. Soc. 108 (2023) 1448–1487, Thm 1.2 (arXiv:2206.03682); M. Suzuki, 'On the Hilbert space derived from the Weil distribution', arXiv:2301.00421 (Canad. J. Math.)
notes: The statement was verified as quoted in Suzuki arXiv:2606.09096 §1.2. It is the imported input of T-91008.

repo_statement: First-Hermite abstract theorem (ZH.17) and countable criterion (ZH.31): a multiset reality criterion via a countable family of positivity tests.
literature_result: For any multiset R of complex numbers with the 4-fold symmetry and mild summability, positivity of λ_n=Σ{1-(1-1/ρ)^n} for all n is equivalent to Re ρ=1/2 for all ρ. λ_n is Weil's functional at explicit test functions, so Li's criterion is a countable restriction of Weil's.
citation: E. Bombieri, J. C. Lagarias, 'Complements to Li's criterion for the Riemann Hypothesis', J. Number Theory 77 (1999) 274–287, Zbl 0972.11079; X.-J. Li, J. Number Theory 65 (1997) 325–333
notes: Same logical shape: an abstract multiset theorem plus a countable Weil-type family. The First-Hermite family (Gaussian first-Hermite squares F_{q,x}F_{q,x}^*) and the terminal-pair/threat-graph argument differ. Searches (arXiv API, zbMATH, one web search) found no prior statement of ZH.29 itself.

repo_statement: ZH.29: RH iff Σ_ρ(γ_ρ-x)^2 e^{-q(γ_ρ-x)^2} ≥ 0 for all q>0 and real x, a Weil square on a two-parameter Schwartz family.
literature_result: Weil's criterion: RH iff W(g*g̃) ≥ 0 for all admissible g.
notes: The forward direction (RH implies positivity) is a special case of Weil's criterion, extended to Schwartz tests. The converse uses a much smaller test family than Weil's, so it is formally stronger. It is still an equivalent of RH, not progress toward it.

repo_statement: First-Hermite wedge (DW.2): unconditional positivity for q ≤ (4-ε)loglog|x|, from the gamma reserve q^{-3/2}log|x| against the phase-blind prime envelope of size q e^{q/4}.
literature_result: Classical explicit-formula arguments: a smooth test of width w at height T has archimedean main term ≍ log T, which dominates the trivially bounded prime sum when the prime support is small. Examples are Littlewood-type zero-detection in short intervals and Selberg/Goldston–Gonek/Carneiro–Chandee–Milinovich bounds via Beurling–Selberg majorants under RH.
citation: J. E. Littlewood (1924) on gaps between zero ordinates; D. A. Goldston, S. M. Gonek, Bull. LMS 39 (2007); E. Carneiro, V. Chandee, M. Milinovich, Math. Ann. (2013)
notes: The wedge is the Gaussian-test incarnation of 'archimedean term beats trivial prime bound'. Its novelty is the specific first-Hermite positivity statement, not the mechanism.

repo_statement: Section 10 seven-point inequality (S1) and the corrected 269 scalar R=(1345000H0-2680)/1340003 ≈ 0.6730085.
literature_result: Knausgård states a 'certificate principle for the critical line' (Thm 5.1): if (x,b) satisfies tr φ2(U_ε)-n ≥ xn-b·spread(Y)-ω(ε)n-C2, then liminf N_0^s(T)/N(T) ≥ (2-C(f)-b)/(1-x). He states that ainta's constant is its value at (x,b)=(4997/1345000, 2680/1345000), which is exactly the repo's R. He lists 0.67300 (ainta) among unrefereed values and proves s0=1669159/2478195=0.67353820 unconditionally for simple zeros on the critical line, and liminf N_d/N ≥ 0.83900. Proofs are Lean-checked except that the seven/eight-point searches enter as axioms.
citation: K. M. Knausgård, 'More than 83.9% of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function are distinct and more than 67.35% are simple and on the critical line', arXiv:2610.08965 (2026), Thm 1.3, Thm 5.1, §1; ainta, github.com/ainta/zeta-simple-zeros @040c5e8 (the repo's source)
notes: The scalar is identical to ainta's quoted constant (0.67300). As a proportion it is superseded (repo_weaker) by 0.67353820 in a 2026 preprint, and by other unrefereed values up to 0.673492 that Knausgård lists. The seven-point inequality is one member of a family: Chandru's seven-point (0.67305 at (x,b)=(19/5000,1/500)), trmdy's pressure 1/2736 with δ=891/200000 (imported as Prop. 6 in Knausgård arXiv:2609.33043), and Knausgård's eight-point frames.

repo_statement: H0=3/2-x cot x with x=1/√2 (RECORD_ARITHMETIC §1), the base constant of the simple-zero deduction.
literature_result: Montgomery–Taylor window constant C0=3/2-(1/√2)cot(1/√2)=0.6725007... It is now an unconditional lower bound for the proportion of simple zeros on the critical line (Alpöge–Furman, via a rank–trace inequality on a finite compression of Weil's Hermitian form and Sylvester inertia; Lamzouri, via a Hilbert space inequality). Both use the unconditional Montgomery theorem of Baluyot–Goldston–Suriajaya–Turnage-Butterbaugh.
citation: L. Alpöge, R. Furman, arXiv:2608.13637 (2026); Y. Lamzouri, arXiv:2609.02882 (2026) eq. (1.1); S. A. C. Baluyot et al., Acta Arith. 214 (2024) 357–376 (arXiv:2306.04799); H. L. Montgomery, Proc. Symp. Pure Math. 24 (1973)
notes: The repo's 'not a scalar-only zeta theorem' caution matches the literature: the deduction from (x,b) to a proportion is the certificate principle, with BGST/Alpöge–Furman inputs.

repo_statement: REFUTATION.FREDHOLM.FIXED_DEGREE_HIGH_CARRIER: each fixed degree becomes positive at high carrier and is asymptotically blind to RH; Q4 fixed/sublinear-order Hermite positivity is kept distinct from all-order.
literature_result: For each fixed degree d, the Jensen polynomials J^{d,n} of Ξ's Taylor data are hyperbolic for all sufficiently large shifts n, because they converge to Hermite polynomials (all d ≤ 8 proven). Farmer argues such fixed-degree/large-shift results give no evidence for RH and proposes criteria for useful RH-equivalences.
citation: M. Griffin, K. Ono, L. Rolen, D. Zagier, PNAS 116 (2019) 11103–11110, arXiv:1902.07321; D. W. Farmer, 'Jensen polynomials are not a plausible route to proving the Riemann Hypothesis', arXiv:2008.07206
notes: Same phenomenon: fixed-order positivity is forced by a universal Hermite/Gaussian limit and is RH-blind. This supports the repo's firewall.

repo_statement: REFUTATION.BROWNIAN.COFINAL_STABILITY (selected-prime/vertical-limit Bohr instability), and O2's use of cos ≤ 1 for the prime comb.
literature_result: Lemma 3.2: sup_t Σ_{log n<2L}2Λ(n)n^{-1/2}cos(t log n)=A_L. The supremum is approached at arbitrarily large t by Weyl equidistribution of (t log p)_p, using Q-linear independence of log p. Hence the crude constant is optimal among pointwise comb bounds. Remark 3.3 shows that a per-prime 'sharpening' bounds the comb in the wrong direction.
citation: Zhu, arXiv:2608.24827v2, Lemma 3.2, Remark 3.3; classical Kronecker/Bohr
notes: It is a precise modern statement of the same Bohr/Kronecker obstruction the repo records for finite Brownian producers.

repo_statement: Suzuki/Hardy delayed causal-wavelet reformulation and the 'scattering isometry' viewpoint (T-91008, L-91035).
literature_result: To a global field K, Burnol associates a Lax–Phillips scattering that is causal iff RH holds for all abelian L-functions of K. This is an adelic Nyman–Beurling-type closure problem.
citation: J.-F. Burnol, 'An adelic causality problem related to abelian L-functions', J. Number Theory 87 (2001) 253–269, arXiv:math/0001013
notes: It is earlier precedent for RH-equivalent causality/scattering reformulations.

repo_statement: OPEN.WEIL.CORRECTED_ARITHMETIC_FLOOR includes an 'odd half-line sign' alternative.
literature_result: Yoshida [Prop. 1]: QW(v) ≥ 0 for all nonzero odd v in C_c^∞ implies RH. The even-sector analogue implies RH except possibly for real zeros. Zhu certifies the odd sector separately at support 1.6, where the pole term changes sign.
citation: Yoshida 1992 Prop. 1 (via Suzuki arXiv:2606.09096 §1.1); Zhu arXiv:2608.24827 §6
notes: Cite Yoshida for the sufficiency of the odd sector. The repo's 'odd half-line sign' normalization was not compared in detail.

repo_statement: Conjunctive APIs: Perron absorption (fixed nonnegative subcritical matrix absorbs coupled negative masses) and regional row/column Schur pairing.
literature_result: M-matrix/Neumann-series lemma: if A ≥ 0 entrywise with spectral radius < 1, then (I-A)^{-1}=ΣA^k ≥ 0, so x ≤ Ax+b with x ≥ 0 gives x ≤ (I-A)^{-1}b. The Schur test bounds an operator from weighted row/column sums.
citation: A. Berman, R. J. Plemmons, Nonnegative Matrices in the Mathematical Sciences (1979), Ch. 6; I. Schur, J. reine angew. Math. 140 (1911)
notes: These are classical tools. The open content is entirely in the literal native source estimates (OPEN.CONJ.*), which the APIs do not supply.

repo_statement: Dissipation identity -Re⟨f,Lf⟩=(1/2)∫||f-D_tf||^2dν for a jump generator Lf=∫(D_tf-f)dν.
literature_result: Beurling–Deny/Lévy–Khintchine: the jump part of a symmetric Dirichlet form, and compound-Poisson generators, have energy (1/2)∫||f-D_tf||^2 dν.
citation: M. Fukushima, Y. Oshima, M. Takeda, Dirichlet Forms and Symmetric Markov Processes (2nd ed. 2011), §3.2
notes: It is a classical identity and needs no new review beyond normalization.

obstruction: Pointwise-envelope certificates of window Weil positivity need frequency resolution T1(L)=2πe^{A_L} with A_L ~ 4e^L, i.e. doubly exponential in L. No pointwise bound on the prime comb lowers this, because sup of the comb equals A_L.
citation: Zhu, arXiv:2608.24827v2, Theorem 1.4 and Lemma 3.2 (unconditional)
how_it_constrains: The repo's O2 coercivity uses exactly the crude comb bound (cos ≤ 1, i.e. Q_X), so its Schur block grows doubly exponentially in L. From the O2 conditions (S_m ≥ 7+2Q_X, π^2(K+1)^2/L^2 ≥ 2C_m+7/2) I computed the minimal K: about 96 at L=1, 1.2e3 at L=1.5, 1.2e4 at L=2, 1.4e7 at L=3, 1.6e12 at L=4 (my arithmetic from the repo's displayed inequalities; the repo uses K=101 at L=1). An 'unbounded prescribed family of full windows' cannot be reached by this envelope. Any all-L argument needs signed cancellation in the prime comb.

obstruction: The positive margin of window Weil positivity collapses super-exponentially. ε_λ ≤ Cδ_4(λ)(log λ)^3 with δ_n(λ) ~ c_nλ^{2n+1}e^{-4πλ^2} is stated as a theorem (Connes–Kastoris), log-window half-width log λ. Zhu proves λ*(L) ≤ exp(-Le^L) under RH and measures 10^-283 at L=2.
citation: Andrews–Connes–La Gatta arXiv:2611.13129, eq. (4) and Thm 3.2 (citing Kastoris, zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.22864295); Zhu arXiv:2608.24827 conditional theorem and Table 3
how_it_constrains: A lower certificate for a large window must resolve astronomically small margins unless the target is relaxed (see tool T2: ε_L ≥ -η(L), η→0). Numerical positivity at moderate L says little about uniformity. Float64 evaluation of the geometric side produces spurious negative eigenvalues (Zhu §10; Groskin's inconclusive band).

obstruction: Finite Galerkin truncations certify only within a fixed band. An eigenvalue in [-B_T,0) of the archimedean-cutoff matrix certifies nothing, and band-N positivity is not continuum positivity.
citation: Groskin, arXiv:2607.02828v3, Cor. 3.3
how_it_constrains: This confirms the repo's rule that positive Galerkin S_m are upper approximations. Band-limited certificates from the CvS/CCM literature cannot be imported as the repo's continuum lower certificate.

obstruction: Newman's conjecture holds: Λ ≥ 0. For every t<0 the heat-flow deformation H_t of Ξ has non-real zeros.
citation: B. Rodgers, T. Tao, 'The de Bruijn–Newman constant is non-negative', Forum Math. Pi 8 (2020) e6, arXiv:1801.05914; Polymath15, Res. Math. Sci. 6 (2019) 31 (Λ ≤ 0.22)
how_it_constrains: The repo's abstract First-Hermite theorem (ZH.17) applies to the zero multiset of H_t, which is conjugation-invariant, in a strip and of subquadratic count (my inference). So for every t<0, M_{Z_t}(q,x)<0 for some (q,x). A proof of the First-Hermite inequality, or of any heat-type positivity, must use an input destroyed by arbitrarily small backward de Bruijn–Newman deformation, such as the exact Euler product or Λ(n). Functional equation, Gaussian decay, zero-counting asymptotics and 'gamma reserve versus envelope' arguments cannot suffice. RH is 'barely true'.

obstruction: Quasi-RH barrier at the constant-four line. The repo's own source says the constant 4 is 1/(max off-line depth)^2=1/(1/2)^2. By the terminal-pair asymptotic (ZH.3), an off-line zero at depth y0 makes M negative at q ≈ loglog|x|/y0^2. Uniform positivity for q ≤ (4+δ)loglog|x| would therefore (heuristically) exclude zeros with β>1/2+1/√(4+δ), a zero-free strip Re s>1-η(δ).
citation: PR #385 GROWING_RESOLUTION_FIRST_HERMITE_WEDGE.md §1 (DW.4) and §8; zero-free regions known only of Vinogradov–Korobov width (Ford, Proc. LMS 85 (2002))
how_it_constrains: Crossing the constant-four frontier uniformly in x is plausibly at least as hard as the open quasi-Riemann hypothesis. Zero-density estimates near σ=1 cannot give it pointwise. This sharpens R10: the thin boundary is not only insufficient, it is already beyond current technology. This is a heuristic: a quantitative terminal-pair lemma is needed to make it rigorous.

obstruction: De Branges' positivity conditions, which would imply GRH, fail for the de Branges spaces of ζ and L(s,χ4). Lax–Phillips (Appendix 2 to §7 of 'Scattering theory for automorphic functions', 1976) explained difficulties of scattering approaches.
citation: J. B. Conrey, X.-J. Li, 'A note on some positivity conditions related to zeta and L-functions', IMRN 2000 (arXiv:math/9812166), §1–2
how_it_constrains: Hardy-space/canonical-system positivity statements stronger than RH can simply be false. For the Suzuki/Hardy route, any intermediate domination stronger than the screw/Weil sign (e.g. a specific Douglas/Stinespring contraction with a fixed delay structure) must be checked to be RH-equivalent and not merely sufficient, or it may fail.

obstruction: Euler-product-like systems with positive prime weights and good PNT behaviour need not satisfy RH. Beurling generalized-prime systems have zeta zeros on σ=1-1/log t (Diamond–Montgomery–Vorhauer; Zhang). Functions with the zeta-type functional equation but no Euler product have off-line zeros (Davenport–Heilbronn).
citation: H. G. Diamond, H. L. Montgomery, U. M. A. Vorhauer, Math. Ann. 334 (2006) 1–36; W.-B. Zhang, Math. Ann. 337 (2007) 671–704 (Zbl 1121.11061); H. Davenport, H. Heilbronn, J. London Math. Soc. 11 (1936)
how_it_constrains: Mechanisms whose only arithmetic input is positivity of prime/Jordan weights (positive Poisson colligations, positive c_a(n), positive source atoms) cannot prove the RH-equivalent sign. They need gamma-factor and exact-coefficient fidelity. This supports the repo's REFUTATIONS §1 'keep a literal source identity'.

obstruction: Fixed-degree or fixed-order positivity driven by a universal Hermite/Gaussian limit is RH-blind.
citation: Griffin–Ono–Rolen–Zagier PNAS 2019 (arXiv:1902.07321); Farmer arXiv:2008.07206
how_it_constrains: This supports REFUTATION.FREDHOLM.FIXED_DEGREE_HIGH_CARRIER. It warns that Q4.HEAT.PHASE_LOCKED_SUBLINEAR (fixed/sublinear order) cannot be promoted to all-order positivity by asymptotics alone.

obstruction: Continuity of the window ground-state energy in the window length is analytically delicate. Bombieri's claimed continuity ([2000, Thm 5]) 'calls for a more careful analysis'; Suzuki proves continuity of λ_a by the screw-function expansion.
citation: M. Suzuki, arXiv:2606.09096 §1.1–1.2, Theorem 1.3

repo_statement: finite-robin-foundations.md sections 2-3: H(n)<=n, I(H(n))>=I(n), and every violator n>5040 yields a canonical violator H(n)>5040 (equivalence of existence of violators in all integers vs Hardy-Ramanujan canonical integers).
literature_result: CLMS section 5 'Reduction to Hardy-Ramanujan integers' uses the same object and name. For an exponent pattern e, m(e)=prod p_i^{e_i} is the least integer with that pattern (Lemma 9: max of sigma(n)/n over the pattern is attained at m(e)). Lemma 8 is the swap: for q>p and f>e, sigma(p^f q^e)/(p^f q^e) > sigma(p^e q^f)/(p^e q^f), via Lemma 7. Lemma 10(1): if sigma(n)/n >= e^g loglog n then m(e) satisfies the same. Proposition 1: if Robin holds for all HR integers in [5041,x], it holds for all integers in [5041,x]. HR integers <= x number exp((1+o(1)) 2pi sqrt(log x/(3 loglog x))) (Hardy-Ramanujan 1917).
citation: Y.-J. Choie, N. Lichiardopol, P. Moree, P. Sole, 'On Robin's criterion for the Riemann hypothesis', J. Theor. Nombres Bordeaux 19 (2007) (journal-ref on arXiv v2: 351-366); arXiv:math/0604314v2, Section 5, Proposition 1, Lemmas 7-10.
notes: Same map (m(e)=H(n)), same Hardy-Ramanujan name, same 5040 threshold, nonstrict violation convention. Lemma 10(1) is the repo's pointwise transfer. In the arXiv text, the Proposition 1 proof only invokes Lemma 10(2). It does not explicitly treat an n>=5041 whose minimal representative m(e)<=5040 is itself one of the 5040-or-below exceptions. The repo's 5583-threshold barrier closes exactly that case. Alternatively, such an n must share 5040's pattern (4,2,1,1), and every n != 5040 with that pattern has I(n) <= I(7920) ~ 3.66 < e^g loglog5041 ~ 3.817. This is a presentational gap, not an error in the statement. Recommend the repo cite this as the source of sections 2-3.

repo_statement: Sections 2-3 (same transform, even the same letter H) and the reduction 'Robin for all canonical h>5040 implies Robin for all n>5040'.
literature_result: Theorem 2.3 (Multiplicity Permutation): swapping exponents a<b of primes p<q decreases n and increases s(n)=sigma(n)/n. Vojak defines A(n) (sort exponents) and H(n) (first primes, sorted exponents), proves H(n)<=n and s(H(n))>=s(n), and states Theorem 2.4: if Robin holds for all Hardy-Ramanujan numbers >5040, it holds for all integers >5040.
citation: R. Vojak, 'On numbers satisfying Robin's inequality, properties of the next counterexample and improved specific bounds', arXiv:2005.09307v1 (2020; zbMATH lists it as a preprint), Theorems 2.3 and 2.4.
notes: The statement is the contrapositive of the repo's (1)=>(2). The printed proof ('If H(n) satisfies Robin's inequality, so does n') likewise leaves the case H(n)<=5040 implicit. The repo's barrier makes it explicit. The paper appears to be unrefereed.

repo_statement: Section 3: existence of a canonical (Hardy-Ramanujan) violator whenever a violator exists.
literature_result: Theorem 3: if there is any counterexample to Robin's inequality, the least one is superabundant. Proof: no counterexample exists in 5040<n<=10080 (known computation, and 10080 is SA). For a least counterexample n>10080 that is not SA, take k with 10080<=k<n and sigma(k)/k>=sigma(n)/n; k is then a smaller counterexample. SA numbers have nonincreasing exponents on consecutive primes (Alaoglu-Erdos 1944, Theorem 1), so SA is a subset of HR.
citation: A. Akbary, Z. Friggstad, 'Superabundant numbers and the Riemann hypothesis', Amer. Math. Monthly 116 (2009) 273-275, Theorem 3 (author copy www.cs.uleth.ca/~akbary/07-0300.pdf; zbMATH 1229.11116).
notes: As an existence statement the repo's reduction is implied by AF plus Alaoglu-Erdos, with SA a much thinner subset of HR. AF's finite barrier [5041,10080] plays the same role as the repo's [5041,5582]. The repo's pointwise statement (every violator n gives the violator H(n)) is not implied by AF, which concerns only the least violator.

repo_statement: Section 3 boundary: 'Canonical does not mean colossally abundant'; the canonical search domain is complete but infinite.
literature_result: Robin 1984, Proposition 1 of Section 3: if 3<=N<=n<=N' with N,N' consecutive colossally abundant numbers, then G(n)=sigma(n)/(n loglog n) <= max(G(N),G(N')). Hence if any Robin counterexample exists, a CA counterexample exists. The proof is elementary: log I is bounded by a linear function of log n via the CA inequality with the common parameter eps, and -log(log t) is convex. Robin also checked G(N)<e^g numerically for all 5041<N<55440 and for every CA N>=55440 with P+(N)<20000.
citation: G. Robin, 'Grandes valeurs de la fonction somme des diviseurs et hypothese de Riemann', J. Math. Pures Appl. (9) 63 (1984) 187-213 (zbMATH 0516.10036), Section 3, Proposition 1. Restated in Nazardonyavi-Yakubovich arXiv:1211.2147 (eq. 4.23), Lagarias arXiv:math/0008177 section 2, Nicolas-Sondow arXiv:1211.6944 section 1.
notes: CA numbers form a one-parameter family; the number <= x is about log x/loglog x. HR integers grow like exp(c sqrt(log x/loglog x)). As a reduction for finite certification, the CA route is exponentially more efficient than canonical-tree traversal. The original JMPA text was not accessible; the statement is consistent across three independent secondary sources.

repo_statement: Finite barrier: no Robin violation in [5041,5582], with I(5040)=403/105 the unique maximum on [1,5040].
literature_result: Robin 1984 checked all integers 5041<N<55440 numerically (per Nicolas-Sondow). Akbary-Friggstad cite no counterexample in 5040<n<=10080. Vojak Theorem 3.5 covers none in 5041<n<=116144. Briggs 2006 checked CA numbers up to 10^(10^10). Morrill-Platt Theorem 13 proves Robin's inequality for all 5040<n<=10^(10^13.11485) by re-implementing Briggs's CA algorithm in 100-bit interval arithmetic, using Robin's CA interpolation. The unique-maximum fact is equivalent to 5040 being superabundant (OEIS A004394; it is in AF's list of the first 20 SA numbers).
citation: Morrill & Platt, 'Robin's inequality for 20-free integers', Integers 21 (2021) A28 (arXiv:1809.10813v4), Theorem 13 and Corollary 14. Briggs, 'Abundant numbers and the Riemann hypothesis', Experiment. Math. 15 (2006) 251-256 (zbMATH 1149.11041). Nicolas-Sondow, Contemp. Math. 627 (2014) 145-156 (arXiv:1211.6944). Akbary-Friggstad 2009, proof of Theorem 3.

Briggs is secondary: the original expmath.org link is now a spam domain and the Project Euclid PDF was not retrievable. The repo's value is a self-contained exact/directed certificate of a small fragment, plus the exact 5582/5583 threshold. I reproduced the maxima with exact rationals and the thresholds in double precision (3.838090 < 3.838095 < 3.838127); this was not directed arithmetic.

repo_statement: Section 2 proof: G(t)=F_b(t)/F_a(t) is increasing on t>0 for b>a (exponent-inversion removal); sorted exponents on consecutive primes maximize I for a given exponent multiset.
literature_result: Alaoglu-Erdos 1944 Theorem 1: a superabundant n = 2^{k2} 3^{k3} ... p^{kp} has k2>=k3>=...>=kp, with kp=1 except n=4,36. Ramanujan 1915 proves the analogous monotonicity for highly composite numbers. CLMS Lemma 7: (1-x^-e)/(1-x^-f) is strictly decreasing on (1,inf) for e>f>0, which is the same function as the repo's G evaluated at t=1/x.
citation: L. Alaoglu, P. Erdos, 'On highly composite and similar numbers', Trans. AMS 56 (1944) 448-469 (zbMATH 0061.07903), Theorem 1. S. Ramanujan, 'Highly composite numbers', Proc. LMS (2) 14 (1915) 347-409. CLMS 2007, Lemmas 7-8.

repo_statement: Section 4: nested prefix-level encoding l_r=#{i:b_i>=r}, with N_tail=R prod_r Q_{l_r}.
literature_result: The classical representation of CA numbers as products of primorials: N(eps) = prod_{k=1}^{K} prod_{p<x_k(eps)} p, where x_k is defined by F(x_k,k)=eps ('N is a product of primorials'). Morrill-Platt write their final checked n as 29996208012611# * 7662961# * ... * (3#)^10 * 2^19. The level lengths are the conjugate partition of the exponent partition.
citation: Caveney, Nicolas, Sondow, 'On SA, CA, and GA numbers', Ramanujan J. 29 (2012) 359-384 (arXiv:1112.6010), eqs. (7)-(11). Morrill-Platt 2021, proof of Theorem 13.
notes: The repo's g_{i,r}=(q^{r+1}-1)/(q(q^r-1)) equals 1+1/(q+...+q^r), so log g_{i,r}/log q_i = F(q_i,r), exactly the Alaoglu-Erdos/Robin critical-parameter function.

repo_statement: Section 5 / R6: powered envelope I(...)^d <= (I_P I(R))^d M0^a V, with V a nested backward DP over levels with certified caps.
literature_result: The colossally abundant inequality: for every eps>0, sigma(n)/n^{1+eps} <= sigma(N_eps)/N_eps^{1+eps}, maximized by Alaoglu-Erdos/Ramanujan's explicit product. Equivalently I(n) <= I(N_eps)(n/N_eps)^eps, which is the Lagrangian relaxation of max I(n) subject to n<=B. Robin 1983 treats the analogous problem for d(n) (highly composite numbers) with three tools: Lagrangian relaxation (PR)_lambda, whose solutions are the superior HC numbers (Everett's theorem); a dynamic programme over primes with an exponent upper-bound vector ('vecteur majoration', i.e. caps); and Nicolas's 'benefit' method to fill gaps between relaxation solutions.
citation: G. Robin, 'Methodes d'optimisation pour un probleme de theorie des nombres', RAIRO Inform. Theor. 17(3) (1983) 239-247 (numdam ITA_1983__17_3_239_0), sections 1-3. H. Everett, Oper. Res. 11 (1963) 399-417. J.-L. Nicolas, Asterisque 24-25 (1975) 325-333 and 38-39 (1976) 169-182. Alaoglu-Erdos 1944, Theorem 10 (via Lagarias 2002 eq. (2.3)).
notes: With eps=a/d, the repo's envelope is the Everett/Lagrangian dual bound localized to a fixed-prefix, capped subtree, in exact rationals. Robin 1983 was fulltext_read; the Alaoglu-Erdos CA formula is via Lagarias and CNS. My own derivation, checked exactly: since F(q,r) decreases in both q and r, w_{i,r}=g_{i,r}^d/q_i^a>1 holds on an initial segment of i that shrinks with r. The nesting constraint therefore never binds, and V = prod_{r=2}^{A} prod_{i<=n_r} max(1, g_{i,r}^d q_i^{-a}), i.e. the classical separable CA solution. Exact-rational comparison of the DP and this closed form on 300 random instances: 0 mismatches. On the R6 fixture: V~91.216, U^{1/64}~3.8985 < 3.9.

Equally, RH <=> Robin holds on all SA numbers >5040 (Akbary-Friggstad) <=> on all CA numbers >5040 (Robin Proposition 1).

repo_statement: OPEN_CUTS section 2 requested output: 'a lemma with explicit dependence on support, exponent ... parameters, showing where an existing bound remains uniform'.
literature_result: Exponent-cap results, uniform in (unbounded) support: Robin holds for all t-free n>5040 with t=5 (CLMS Theorem 5), t=7 (Sole-Planat), t=11 (Broughan-Trudgian), t=20 (Morrill-Platt Theorem 2) and t=21 (Axler Theorem 1.2). Hence RH <=> Robin for all 21-full n (Axler Corollary 2.5). Single-prime valuation conditions: Robin holds for n>5040 if v2(n)<=19 (Hertlein Theorem 1), or if v2(n)<=20, or v5(n)<=8, or vp(n)<=4 for some prime 11<p<=19, <=3 for some 19<p<=41, <=2 for some 41<p<=139, or =1 for some 139<p<=1777 (Axler Theorem 1.4). CLMS also covers odd n>9, squarefree n not in {2,3,5,6,10,30}, and squarefull n beyond a finite list.
citation: Morrill-Platt, Integers 21 (2021) A28, Theorem 2. C. Axler, 'On Robin's inequality', Ramanujan J. 61 (2023) 909-919 (arXiv:2110.13478), Theorems 1.2 and 1.4. A. Hertlein, Integers 18 (2018) A71 (arXiv:1612.05186), Theorems 1-3. Broughan-Trudgian, Integers 15 (2015) A12. Sole-Planat, Integers 12 (2012) 301-309. CLMS 2007, Theorems 1, 2, 4, 5.
notes: These are existing instances of exactly the requested output type. In canonical language, any canonical violator has b_1>=21, and by monotonicity all exponents up to 1777 satisfy Axler's floors. The constraints rest on explicit prime-counting inputs (Dusart; Platt-Trudgian RH verification to 3*10^12) and must be labelled as imported.

repo_statement: Section 3 boundary 'support size and exponents remain unbounded'; OPEN_CUTS support-dependence.
literature_result: Vojak Theorem 1.4 / Corollary 1.5: with M(k)=exp(e^-g f(N_k)) - log N_k (where f(N_k)=N_k/phi(N_k) and N_k is the k-th primorial), an n with omega(n)=k satisfies Robin if some a_i >= 1+M(k)/log q_i, and every such n satisfies Robin if M(k)<=0. Theorem 1.6: the least counterexample c is SA, has omega(c)>=969,672,728, fewer than omega(c)/14 non-unit exponents, and p_{omega(c)}<log c. CLMS Lemma 11: the least t-free counterexample has P(n)<log n.
citation: Vojak, arXiv:2005.09307, Theorems 1.3, 1.4, 1.6, Corollary 1.5, Theorem 3.5. CLMS 2007, Lemma 11.
notes: Elementary consequence: since I(h) < N_k/phi(N_k) when omega(h)=k, any violator with support k has log h < exp(e^-g N_k/phi(N_k)). So each fixed-support canonical class contains only finitely many candidates; e.g. k=4 gives h<~1.16*10^5, matching Vojak's 116144. The unboundedness lies only in support size. M(k)<=0 is exactly failure of Nicolas's inequality at N_k. Vojak's omega(c) bound used Briggs's 10^(10^10). Rerunning his inequality with Morrill-Platt's range gives log p_omega > ~31.0, omega(c) >~ 10^12 (my floating-point extrapolation, not certified).

repo_statement: Arithmetic route organization (prime support plus exponent pattern; canonical reduction as the sigma-analogue of a minimal-n reduction).
literature_result: Nicolas 1983: RH <=> N_k/phi(N_k) > e^g loglog N_k for all primorials N_k (k>=1). If RH is false, the inequality holds for infinitely many k and fails for infinitely many k. For n/phi(n), which depends only on the prime support, the minimal-n representative of a support size is the primorial, so the criterion collapses to a one-parameter family. For sigma the analogous one-parameter family is the CA numbers.
citation: J.-L. Nicolas, 'Petites valeurs de la fonction d'Euler', J. Number Theory 17 (1983) 375-388 (zbMATH 0521.10039). Restated in Nazardonyavi-Yakubovich arXiv:1211.2147 (eq. 1.5) and Nicolas-Sondow arXiv:1211.6944.
notes: The original JNT text was not fetched.

repo_statement: Section 3: equivalent search domains for a Robin violation.
literature_result: Further RH-equivalent thin subsequences. Extremely abundant (XA) numbers: the least counterexample, if any, is XA; RH <=> XA is infinite (NY Theorems 2.3-2.4). Extraordinary (GA1 and GA2) numbers: RH <=> 4 is the only extraordinary number, and if RH fails, the least N>5040 attaining max G is extraordinary (CNS 2011). Wu: RH <=> Robin for all CA2 numbers >5040 (a subset of CA). Lagarias: RH <=> sigma(n) <= H_n + exp(H_n) log H_n for all n.

obstruction: If RH is false, Robin's inequality fails for infinitely many n, by a secondary-term margin. There exist 0<beta<1/2 (any 1-b<beta<1/2, with b=Re(rho)>1/2) and C>0 such that sigma(n) >= e^g n loglog n + C n loglog n/(log n)^beta infinitely often.
citation: Robin 1984, Section 4, Proposition 1, as restated in Lagarias, arXiv:math/0008177, Proposition 3.2.
how_it_constrains: A theorem covering the whole unbounded canonical tail is RH itself. No 'complete infinite pruning argument' weaker than RH can exist. Any proposed unconditional tail theorem must contain RH-strength analytic input, i.e. a bound on prime counts at the scale x^{1/2+o(1)}.
evidence_level: fulltext_read (Lagarias restatement; Robin original not accessed)

obstruction: Under RH the Robin margin on the extremal (SA/CA) numbers tends to zero: limsup (sigma(n)/n - e^g loglog n) sqrt(log n) <= -e^g(2sqrt2 - 4 - g + log 4pi) ~ -1.393 (Ramanujan, assuming RH). The explicit form is sigma(n)/n <= e^g(loglog n - 2(sqrt2-1)/sqrt(log n) + S_1(log n) + O(...)), where S_1 is a sum over zeta zeros.
citation: S. Ramanujan, 'Highly composite numbers', annotated by J.-L. Nicolas and G. Robin, Ramanujan J. 1 (1997) 119-153 (zbMATH 0917.11043), sections 59-71; restated in Nicolas-Sondow arXiv:1211.6944 section 1, CNS arXiv:1110.5078 Proposition 1, Axler arXiv:2110.13478 final remark.
how_it_constrains: Finite pruning and envelopes with a fixed relative margin cannot close the tail. The margin shrinks like (log n)^{-1/2} and oscillates with the zeros through S_1.

obstruction: For every fixed n0, limsup_{a->inf} G(a n0) = e^g. Any subtree with a fixed prefix and an unrestricted continuation has no margin. A margin exists only once continuation exponents are capped, and with cap A the asymptotic margin is about a factor prod(1-p^{-A-1}), which tends to 1 as A grows.
citation: Caveney-Nicolas-Sondow, Ramanujan J. 29 (2012) 359-384 (arXiv:1112.6010), Fact 2 (citing CNS 2011, Lemma 10).
how_it_constrains: A subtree tail lemma must be stated per (prefix, cap A). Uniformity in A is equivalent to RH, because every n is t-free for some t.

obstruction: The t-free (Sole-Planat Psi_t) method stalls with current explicit inputs. Morrill-Platt report that both their finite-range and asymptotic bounds exceed 1 at t=21. citation: Morrill-Platt 2021, Section 5 'Comments'. Axler 2023, Theorem 1.2.
how_it_constrains: Exponent-uniform 'tail lemmas' are capped by the precision of explicit PNT and Mertens bounds. Pushing t up by one requires better explicit inputs; no t-free argument reaches unbounded exponents.

repo_statement: L-99613: all-x positivity of the smoothed signed sum H^{[m]}, m>=2 (effective Dirichlet exponent sigma=(m+1)/2>=3/2).
literature_result: For every integer q>=1, real sigma>=1, integer k>=1 and X>=1: 0 <= sum_{n<=X,(n,q)=1} mu(n) n^{-sigma} log^k(X/n) <= 1.00303 (q/phi(q)) (k+(sigma-1)log X)(log X)^{k-1}. The case k=1, sigma=1 is Lemma 4.1: 0 <= sum mu(n)/n log(X/n) <= 1.00303 q/phi(q). The paper attributes the sigma=1 non-negativity to Pólya (1919) and Turán (1948, §25). The sigma>1 case is deduced by expanding X^eps into log-moments, which transfers positivity upward in sigma.
citation: O. Ramaré and S. Zuniga Alterman, 'Möbius function and primes: an identity factory with applications', arXiv:2312.05138v3, Theorem 1.2 (p.2-3), Lemma 4.1 and proof of Thm 1.2 (p.9-10); G. Pólya, Jahresber. DMV 28 (1919) 31-40; P. Turán, Danske Vid. Selsk. Mat.-Fys. Medd. 24 (1948).
notes: Both are all-X positivity statements for smoothed Möbius sums. In both, the limiting main term is strictly positive and the remainder decays, so neither touches RH scale. The literature result sits closer to the critical line in sigma (sigma=1, log-Riesz kernel) than SHARP m=2 (sigma=3/2). The kernel T^m and the 67-modified beta differ, so the relation is not 'identical'. The RZA transfer runs from sigma=1 to sigma>1, the opposite of the m=2 -> m=1 descent the repo needs.

repo_statement: L-99613 method: labelled-level contraction kM_k <= S M_{k-1}, with subunit prime mass S<1, implies a positive alternating sum.
literature_result: This is classical inclusion-exclusion with Poisson-type level bounds M_k <= S^k M_0/k! (Brun pure sieve / Bonferroni truncation). With a sharp cutoff the same double counting gives sum_{n<=x} mu(n) n^{-sigma} >= 1 - sum_{p<=x} p^{-sigma} > 0 for all x whenever P(sigma)=sum_p p^{-sigma}<1, i.e. sigma>1.399433.
citation: Brun's pure sieve, e.g. H. Halberstam and H.-E. Richert, Sieve Methods (1974), Ch. 2. The mu(n)n^{-sigma} corollary is folklore; no published statement was located in arXiv/zbMATH/web searches.
notes: The analyst re-derived the mechanism; SHARP is this argument with the monotone factor T(y)/sqrt y in [1,4). The method's own threshold for SHARP is sum_p p^{-(m+1)/2}+67^{-(m+1)/2}<1. By mpmath primezeta this holds iff (m+1)/2>1.401034, i.e. m>m*≈1.80207. The same proof therefore appears to cover 1.8021<m<2 as well. This observation is unreviewed.

repo_statement: L-99613 (content beyond eventual positivity).
literature_result: For sigma>1, sum beta(n)n^{-sigma}=(1-67^{-sigma})/zeta(sigma)>0 with absolute convergence. Dominated convergence gives x^{-m/2}H^{[m]}(x) -> 4^m(1-67^{-(m+1)/2})/zeta((m+1)/2)>0 for every fixed m>1. Eventual positivity for each fixed m>1 is therefore soft. The limit degenerates like 4(1-1/67)(m-1)/2 as m decreases to 1.
citation: Standard Dirichlet-series facts (e.g. Montgomery-Vaughan, Multiplicative Number Theory I, CUP 2007, §1.3); analyst derivation.
notes: The theorem's genuine content is the all-x statement with an elementary proof. Uniformity as m decreases to 1 must fail at RH scale, consistent with the repo's 'critical wall'. Exploratory grid scans of H^{[m]} on [1,4000] for m in {1,...,1.8,2}, and of H_1 on [1,1e7], found the minimum 1 attained at x=1. These are finite-range scans, not certificates.

literature_result: Differentiating Riesz/typical means lowers the order. For example, C_k(x)=sum_{n<=x} a_n(x-n)^k satisfies C_k'=kC_{k-1}, and logarithmic typical means behave analogously. L-99940 is the same mechanism for the kernel T(y)^2/y, using y d/dy(T^2/y)=3T/y.
citation: G. H. Hardy and M. Riesz, The General Theory of Dirichlet's Series, CUP 1915, Ch. IV (typical means).
notes: An exact identity of a classical type. The repo correctly records that it supplies no estimate.

repo_statement: L-99943/L-99944 and CURRENT_RESULTS §3: subpower one-sided negative mass of a fixed reciprocal-zeta detector implies RH; for H_1 this is an equivalence.
literature_result: Landau's lemma (MV Lemma 15.1): an eventually one-signed integrand has a Mellin transform that is singular at its real abscissa. Corollary: eventual constant sign of L(x)=sum lambda(n) implies RH. Littlewood: RH iff M(x)=O(x^{1/2+eps}). For L_alpha(x)=sum_{n<=x} lambda(n)n^{-alpha}, alpha in [0,1/2]: RH implies L_alpha(x)=O(x^{1/2-alpha+eps}), and that estimate for a single alpha implies RH.
citation: Montgomery and Vaughan, MNT I (2007), Lemma 15.1, as quoted in P. Humphries, arXiv:1108.1524, Lemma 1.2 and Cor. 1.3; M. J. Mossinghoff and T. S. Trudgian, 'Between the problems of Pólya and Turán', J. Aust. Math. Soc. 93 (2012) 157-171 (zbMATH 1305.11076); Titchmarsh, Theory of the Riemann Zeta-Function, §14.25.
notes: The L^1-negative-mass version and the specific detector are the repo's own; the template is classical. As the repo itself states, this is a reformulation, not independent progress.

repo_statement: Critical SHARP detector H_1(x)=4sqrt x sum_{n<=x} beta(n)/n - 3 sum_{n<=x} beta(n)/sqrt n.
literature_result: MMT define the 'apparent bias' of F(x)/sqrt x as the constant term produced by Dirichlet-series poles; for example L(x)/sqrt x has apparent bias 1/zeta(1/2). Their Theorem 3 (after Tanaka) shows unconditionally that liminf F/sqrt x < b < limsup F/sqrt x for fake mu's with f(p)=-1, f(p^2)=1. The method is Landau's lemma applied at the first zero.
citation: G. Martin, M. J. Mossinghoff and T. S. Trudgian, 'Fake mu's', Proc. AMS (2023), arXiv:2112.05227, abstract, §1, Theorem 3 and §4 (pp. 13-14).
notes: Analyst computation by Perron residues. Under RH and simple zeros, H_1(x) = b_H + sum_rho x^{i gamma}(1-67^{-rho})(rho+1)/(zeta'(rho)(rho-1)(rho-1/2)) + o(1), with b_H = -3(1-67^{-1/2})/zeta(1/2) = 1.803324. The s=0 term of 4sqrt x sum beta/n vanishes because 1/zeta(1)=0. Exact double-precision evaluation gives a logarithmic average of H_1 over [1e3,1e7] of 1.80067. Over the first 400 zeros, 2 sum |c_rho| = 1.674, tracking the Mertens analogue 2 sum 1/|rho zeta'(rho)| = 1.637.

literature_result:
From Tao's identity, A_P(x) = N_P(x)/x + x^{-1} sum_{d in

repo_statement: OPEN.ARITH.CV (H_1 negative mass) and the sign branch of OPEN.ARITH.ROWS23_NATIVE.
literature_result: Assume RH, LI and J_{-1}(T)<<T. Then L_alpha has a limiting logarithmic distribution and 1/2<=delta(P_alpha)<1 for 0<=alpha<1/2, so both signs occur on sets of positive log density. Under RH and J_{-1}(T)<<T alone, L_{1/2}(x)<=0 outside a set of log density 0; there the log-growing bias dominates. Ng: under RH and J_{-1}(T)<<T, e^{-y/2}M(e^y) has a limiting distribution and the weak Mertens conjecture holds.
citation: P. Humphries, J. Number Theory 133 (2013), arXiv:1108.1524, Theorems 1.5-1.6 (pp.3-4); N. Ng, Proc. LMS 89 (2004), arXiv:math/0310381 (abstract).

repo_statement: L-99940 descent between powers combined with sign criteria.
